description:
The user approved page v1 at 2026-11-18T21:26Z, verbatim via Optimize: "approved; proceed." The user then said: "goals approved; now, dig into the code, and figure out what needs to change, consolidate, fold, clean up, organize, be corrected to get us from where we are to the goal. update the proposal with a concrete plan of action, composed into steps that build inexorably toward the goal." The user then approved page v2, verbatim via Optimize: "approved. proceed." v2 keeps storage order as it is (term order): a one-word key (atom, int, float, pid, ref) is found by word equality, as BEAM does, and order is consulted only to place a new key. Atom ids are not stable, so the v1 decisions on atom order are withdrawn. Page: https://claude.ai/artifact/MmnrdprbWQMF24ejqsUaQL (/Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-map-raw-words.html); measurements https://claude.ai/artifact/KASxGisqvtZNq498dbRi8D. User direction: meet or exceed BEAM in all cases; hand-written optimal arm64 first, then make the compiler emit it. Builder: Optimize. Pass rules are judged on bench and pre-registered on the page.

Step 3a. One find(map, word, kind) returns slot + found and serves the flat, trie-leaf and struct layouts. It is used by put/get/has-key/fetch/delete/update/replace. Map.fetch, get/3, update, replace and take in lib/map.fz search once. Removed: map_key_position, locate_key and StructMap::position. This supersedes the double-lookup proposal (decision 89).

comments.text: Optimize's finding from .5's probes (#750): a single ordered search (kind rank, then the atom-name prefix) is within about 10% of scan-by-equality on lookups and cheaper on builds. So .7 may be one ordered search instead of scan + place. Optimize decides inside .7 with fz numbers.

title: Every map operation finds its key with one find
